lines.text: and rotten, come hither. What ail’st thou, man?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: I have seen two such sights, by sea and by land! But I am not to say it

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: is a sea, for it is now the sky: betwixt the firmament and it, you

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: cannot thrust a bodkin’s point.

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: Why, boy, how is it?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: I would you did but see how it chafes, how it rages, how it takes up

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: the shore! But that’s not to the point. O, the most piteous cry of the

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: poor souls! sometimes to see ’em, and not to see ’em. Now the ship

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: boring the moon with her mainmast, and anon swallowed with yest and

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: froth, as you’d thrust a cork into a hogshead. And then for the land

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: service, to see how the bear tore out his shoulder-bone, how he cried

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: to me for help, and said his name was Antigonus, a nobleman. But to

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: make an end of the ship, to see how the sea flap-dragon’d it: but

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: first, how the poor souls roared, and the sea mocked them, and how the

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: poor gentleman roared, and the bear mocked him, both roaring louder

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: than the sea or weather.

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: Name of mercy, when was this, boy?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Now, now. I have not winked since I saw these sights: the men are not

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: yet cold under water, nor the bear half dined on the gentleman. He’s at

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: it now.

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: Would I had been by to have helped the old man!

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: I would you had been by the ship side, to have helped her: there your

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: charity would have lacked footing.

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: Heavy matters, heavy matters! But look thee here, boy. Now bless

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: thyself: thou met’st with things dying, I with things new-born. Here’s

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: a sight for thee. Look thee, a bearing-cloth for a squire’s child! Look

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: thee here; take up, take up, boy; open’t. So, let’s see. It was told me

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: I should be rich by the fairies. This is some changeling: open’t.

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: What’s within, boy?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: You’re a made old man. If the sins of your youth are forgiven you,

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: you’re well to live. Gold! all gold!

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: This is fairy gold, boy, and ’twill prove so. Up with it, keep it

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: close: home, home, the next way. We are lucky, boy, and to be so still

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: requires nothing but secrecy. Let my sheep go: come, good boy, the next

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: way home.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Go you the next way with your findings. I’ll go see if the bear be gone

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: from the gentleman, and how much he hath eaten. They are never curst

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: but when they are hungry: if there be any of him left, I’ll bury it.

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: That’s a good deed. If thou mayest discern by that which is left of him

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: what he is, fetch me to th’ sight of him.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Marry, will I; and you shall help to put him i’ th’ ground.

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: ’Tis a lucky day, boy, and we’ll do good deeds on ’t.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Time, the Chorus.

lines.speaker: TIME
lines.text: I that please some, try all: both joy and terror

lines.speaker: TIME
lines.text: Of good and bad, that makes and unfolds error,

lines.speaker: TIME
lines.text: Now take upon me, in the name of Time,

lines.speaker: TIME
lines.text: To use my wings. Impute it not a crime

lines.speaker: TIME
lines.text: To me or my swift passage, that I slide

lines.speaker: TIME
lines.text: O’er sixteen years, and leave the growth untried

lines.speaker: TIME
lines.text: Of that wide gap, since it is in my power

lines.speaker: TIME
lines.text: To o’erthrow law, and in one self-born hour

lines.speaker: TIME
lines.text: To plant and o’erwhelm custom. Let me pass

lines.speaker: TIME
lines.text: The same I am, ere ancient’st order was

lines.speaker: TIME
lines.text: Or what is now received. I witness to

lines.speaker: TIME
lines.text: The times that brought them in; so shall I do

lines.speaker: TIME
lines.text: To th’ freshest things now reigning, and make stale

lines.speaker: TIME
lines.text: The glistering of this present, as my tale

lines.speaker: TIME
lines.text: Now seems to it. Your patience this allowing,

lines.speaker: TIME
lines.text: I turn my glass, and give my scene such growing

lines.speaker: TIME
lines.text: As you had slept between. Leontes leaving

lines.speaker: TIME
lines.text: Th’ effects of his fond jealousies, so grieving

lines.speaker: TIME
lines.text: That he shuts up himself, imagine me,

lines.speaker: TIME
lines.text: Gentle spectators, that I now may be

lines.speaker: TIME
lines.text: In fair Bohemia, and remember well,

lines.speaker: TIME
lines.text: I mentioned a son o’ th’ king’s, which Florizel

lines.speaker: TIME
lines.text: I now name to you; and with speed so pace

lines.speaker: TIME
lines.text: To speak of Perdita, now grown in grace

lines.speaker: TIME
lines.text: Equal with wondering. What of her ensues

lines.speaker: TIME
lines.text: I list not prophesy; but let Time’s news

lines.speaker: TIME
lines.text: Be known when ’tis brought forth. A shepherd’s daughter,

lines.speaker: TIME
lines.text: And what to her adheres, which follows after,

lines.speaker: TIME
lines.text: Is th’ argument of Time. Of this allow,

lines.speaker: TIME
lines.text: If ever you have spent time worse ere now;

lines.speaker: TIME
lines.text: If never, yet that Time himself doth say

lines.speaker: TIME
lines.text: He wishes earnestly you never may.
[_Exit._]

scenes.setting: Bohemia. A Room in the palace of Polixenes.

lines.text: Enter Polixenes and Camillo.

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: I pray thee, good Camillo, be no more importunate: ’tis a sickness

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: denying thee anything; a death to grant this.

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: It is fifteen years since I saw my country. Though I have for the most

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: part been aired abroad, I desire to lay my bones there. Besides, the

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: penitent king, my master, hath sent for me; to whose feeling sorrows I

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: might be some allay, or I o’erween to think so,—which is another spur

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: to my departure.

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: As thou lov’st me, Camillo, wipe not out the rest of thy services by

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: leaving me now: the need I have of thee, thine own goodness hath made;

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: better not to have had thee than thus to want thee. Thou, having made

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: me businesses which none without thee can sufficiently manage, must

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: either stay to execute them thyself, or take away with thee the very

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: services thou hast done, which if I have not enough considered (as too

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: much I cannot) to be more thankful to thee shall be my study; and my

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: profit therein the heaping friendships. Of that fatal country Sicilia,

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: prithee speak no more; whose very naming punishes me with the

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: remembrance of that penitent, as thou call’st him, and reconciled king,

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: my brother; whose loss of his most precious queen and children are even

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: now to be afresh lamented. Say to me, when sawest thou the Prince

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: Florizel, my son? Kings are no less unhappy, their issue not being

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: gracious, than they are in losing them when they have approved their

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: virtues.

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: Sir, it is three days since I saw the prince. What his happier affairs

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: may be, are to me unknown, but I have missingly noted he is of late

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: much retired from court, and is less frequent to his princely exercises

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: than formerly he hath appeared.

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: I have considered so much, Camillo, and with some care; so far that I

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: have eyes under my service which look upon his removedness; from whom I

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: have this intelligence, that he is seldom from the house of a most

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: homely shepherd, a man, they say, that from very nothing, and beyond

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: the imagination of his neighbours, is grown into an unspeakable estate.

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: I have heard, sir, of such a man, who hath a daughter of most rare

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: note: the report of her is extended more than can be thought to begin

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: from such a cottage.

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: That’s likewise part of my intelligence: but, I fear, the angle that

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: plucks our son thither. Thou shalt accompany us to the place, where we

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: will, not appearing what we are, have some question with the shepherd;

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: from whose simplicity I think it not uneasy to get the cause of my

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: son’s resort thither. Prithee, be my present partner in this business,

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: and lay aside the thoughts of Sicilia.

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: I willingly obey your command.

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: My best Camillo! We must disguise ourselves.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: The same. A Road near the Shepherd’s cottage.

lines.text: Enter Autolycus, singing.

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: _When daffodils begin to peer,

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: With, hey! the doxy over the dale,

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: Why, then comes in the sweet o’ the year,

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: For the red blood reigns in the winter’s pale._

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: _The white sheet bleaching on the hedge,

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: With, hey! the sweet birds, O, how they sing!

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: Doth set my pugging tooth on edge;

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: For a quart of ale is a dish for a king._

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: _The lark, that tirra-lirra chants,

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: With, hey! with, hey! the thrush and the jay,

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: Are summer songs for me and my aunts,

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: While we lie tumbling in the hay._

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: I have served Prince Florizel, and in my time wore three-pile, but now

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: I am out of service.

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: _But shall I go mourn for that, my dear?

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: The pale moon shines by night:

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: And when I wander here and there,

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: I then do most go right._

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: _If tinkers may have leave to live,

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: And bear the sow-skin budget,

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: Then my account I well may give

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: And in the stocks avouch it._

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: My traffic is sheets; when the kite builds, look to lesser linen. My

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: father named me Autolycus; who being, I as am, littered under Mercury,

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: was likewise a snapper-up of unconsidered trifles. With die and drab I

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: purchased this caparison, and my revenue is the silly cheat. Gallows

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: and knock are too powerful on the highway. Beating and hanging are

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: terrors to me. For the life to come, I sleep out the thought of it. A

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: prize! a prize!
Enter Clown.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Let me see: every ’leven wether tods; every tod yields pound and odd

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: shilling; fifteen hundred shorn, what comes the wool to?
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: If the springe hold, the cock’s mine.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: I cannot do’t without counters. Let me see; what am I to buy for our

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: sheep-shearing feast? “Three pound of sugar, five pound of currants,

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: rice”—what will this sister of mine do with rice? But my father hath

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: made her mistress of the feast, and she lays it on. She hath made me

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: four-and-twenty nosegays for the shearers, three-man song-men all, and

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: very good ones; but they are most of them means and basses, but one

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: puritan amongst them, and he sings psalms to hornpipes. I must have

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: saffron to colour the warden pies; “mace; dates”, none, that’s out of

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: my note; “nutmegs, seven; a race or two of ginger”, but that I may beg;

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: “four pound of prunes, and as many of raisins o’ th’ sun.”
[_Grovelling on the ground._]

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: O that ever I was born!

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: I’ th’ name of me!

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: O, help me, help me! Pluck but off these rags; and then, death, death!

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Alack, poor soul! thou hast need of more rags to lay on thee, rather

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: than have these off.

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: O sir, the loathsomeness of them offends me more than the stripes I

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: have received, which are mighty ones and millions.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Alas, poor man! a million of beating may come to a great matter.

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: I am robbed, sir, and beaten; my money and apparel ta’en from me, and

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: these detestable things put upon me.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: What, by a horseman or a footman?

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: A footman, sweet sir, a footman.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Indeed, he should be a footman by the garments he has left with thee:

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: if this be a horseman’s coat, it hath seen very hot service. Lend me

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: thy hand, I’ll help thee: come, lend me thy hand.
[_Helping him up._]

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: O, good sir, tenderly, O!

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Alas, poor soul!

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: O, good sir, softly, good sir. I fear, sir, my shoulder blade is out.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: How now! canst stand?

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: Softly, dear sir! [_Picks his pocket._] good sir, softly. You ha’ done

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: me a charitable office.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Dost lack any money? I have a little money for thee.

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: No, good sweet sir; no, I beseech you, sir: I have a kinsman not past

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: three-quarters of a mile hence, unto whom I was going. I shall there

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: have money or anything I want. Offer me no money, I pray you; that

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: kills my heart.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: What manner of fellow was he that robbed you?

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: A fellow, sir, that I have known to go about with troll-my-dames. I

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: knew him once a servant of the prince; I cannot tell, good sir, for

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: which of his virtues it was, but he was certainly whipped out of the

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: court.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: His vices, you would say; there’s no virtue whipped out of the court.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: They cherish it to make it stay there; and yet it will no more but

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: abide.

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: Vices, I would say, sir. I know this man well. He hath been since an

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: ape-bearer, then a process-server, a bailiff. Then he compassed a

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: motion of the Prodigal Son, and married a tinker’s wife within a mile

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: where my land and living lies; and, having flown over many knavish

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: professions, he settled only in rogue. Some call him Autolycus.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Out upon him! prig, for my life, prig: he haunts wakes, fairs, and

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: bear-baitings.

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: Very true, sir; he, sir, he; that’s the rogue that put me into this

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: apparel.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Not a more cowardly rogue in all Bohemia. If you had but looked big and

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: spit at him, he’d have run.

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: I must confess to you, sir, I am no fighter. I am false of heart that

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: way; and that he knew, I warrant him.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: How do you now?

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: Sweet sir, much better than I was. I can stand and walk: I will even

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: take my leave of you and pace softly towards my kinsman’s.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Shall I bring thee on the way?

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: No, good-faced sir; no, sweet sir.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Then fare thee well. I must go buy spices for our sheep-shearing.

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: Prosper you, sweet sir!
[_Exit Clown._]

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: Your purse is not hot enough to purchase your spice. I’ll be with you

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: at your sheep-shearing too. If I make not this cheat bring out

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: another, and the shearers prove sheep, let me be unrolled, and my name

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: put in the book of virtue!
[_Sings._]

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: _Jog on, jog on, the footpath way,

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: And merrily hent the stile-a:

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: A merry heart goes all the day,

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: Your sad tires in a mile-a._
[_Exit._]
Enter Florizel and Perdita.

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: These your unusual weeds to each part of you

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: Do give a life, no shepherdess, but Flora

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: Peering in April’s front. This your sheep-shearing

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: Is as a meeting of the petty gods,

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: And you the queen on ’t.

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: Sir, my gracious lord,

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: To chide at your extremes it not becomes me;

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: O, pardon that I name them! Your high self,

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: The gracious mark o’ th’ land, you have obscur’d

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: With a swain’s wearing, and me, poor lowly maid,

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: Most goddess-like prank’d up. But that our feasts

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: In every mess have folly, and the feeders

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: Digest it with a custom, I should blush

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: To see you so attir’d; swoon, I think,

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: To show myself a glass.

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: I bless the time

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: When my good falcon made her flight across

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: Thy father’s ground.

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: Now Jove afford you cause!

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: To me the difference forges dread. Your greatness

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: Hath not been us’d to fear. Even now I tremble

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: To think your father, by some accident,

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: Should pass this way, as you did. O, the Fates!

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: How would he look to see his work, so noble,

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: Vilely bound up? What would he say? Or how

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: Should I, in these my borrow’d flaunts, behold

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: The sternness of his presence?

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: Apprehend

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: Nothing but jollity. The gods themselves,

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: Humbling their deities to love, have taken

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: The shapes of beasts upon them. Jupiter

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: Became a bull and bellow’d; the green Neptune

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: A ram and bleated; and the fire-rob’d god,

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: Golden Apollo, a poor humble swain,

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: As I seem now. Their transformations

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: Were never for a piece of beauty rarer,

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: Nor in a way so chaste, since my desires

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: Run not before mine honour, nor my lusts

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: Burn hotter than my faith.

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: O, but, sir,

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: Your resolution cannot hold when ’tis

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: Oppos’d, as it must be, by the power of the king:

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: One of these two must be necessities,

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: Which then will speak, that you must change this purpose,

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: Or I my life.

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: Thou dearest Perdita,

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: With these forc’d thoughts, I prithee, darken not

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: The mirth o’ th’ feast. Or I’ll be thine, my fair,

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: Or not my father’s. For I cannot be

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: Mine own, nor anything to any, if

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL

lines.text: A fair one are you—well you fit our ages

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: Sir, the year growing ancient,

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: Not yet on summer’s death nor on the birth

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: Of trembling winter, the fairest flowers o’ th’ season

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: Are our carnations and streak’d gillyvors,

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: Which some call nature’s bastards: of that kind

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: Our rustic garden’s barren; and I care not

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: To get slips of them.

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: Wherefore, gentle maiden,

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: Do you neglect them?

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: For I have heard it said

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: There is an art which, in their piedness, shares

lines.text: With great creating nature.

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: Say there be;

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: Yet nature is made better by no mean

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: But nature makes that mean. So, over that art

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: Which you say adds to nature, is an art

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: That nature makes. You see, sweet maid, we marry

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: A gentler scion to the wildest stock,

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: And make conceive a bark of baser kind

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: By bud of nobler race. This is an art

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: Which does mend nature, change it rather, but

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: The art itself is nature.

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: So it is.

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: Then make your garden rich in gillyvors,

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: And do not call them bastards.

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: I’ll not put

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: The dibble in earth to set one slip of them;

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: No more than, were I painted, I would wish

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: This youth should say ’twere well, and only therefore

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: Desire to breed by me. Here’s flowers for you:

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: Hot lavender, mints, savory, marjoram,

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: The marigold, that goes to bed with th’ sun

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: And with him rises weeping. These are flowers

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: Of middle summer, and I think they are given

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: To men of middle age. You’re very welcome.

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: I should leave grazing, were I of your flock,

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: And only live by gazing.

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: Out, alas!

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: You’d be so lean that blasts of January

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: Would blow you through and through. [_To Florizel_] Now, my fair’st

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: friend,

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: I would I had some flowers o’ th’ spring, that might

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: Become your time of day; and yours, and yours,

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: That wear upon your virgin branches yet

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: Your maidenheads growing. O Proserpina,

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: From the flowers now that, frighted, thou let’st fall

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: From Dis’s waggon! daffodils,

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: That come before the swallow dares, and take

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: The winds of March with beauty; violets dim,

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: But sweeter than the lids of Juno’s eyes

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: Or Cytherea’s breath; pale primroses,

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: That die unmarried ere they can behold

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: Bright Phoebus in his strength (a malady

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: Most incident to maids); bold oxlips and

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: The crown imperial; lilies of all kinds,

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: The flower-de-luce being one. O, these I lack,

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: To make you garlands of; and my sweet friend,

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: To strew him o’er and o’er!

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: What, like a corse?

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: No, like a bank for love to lie and play on;

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: Not like a corse; or if, not to be buried,

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: But quick, and in mine arms. Come, take your flowers.

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: Methinks I play as I have seen them do

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: In Whitsun pastorals. Sure this robe of mine

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: Does change my disposition.

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: What you do

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: Still betters what is done. When you speak, sweet,

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: I’d have you do it ever. When you sing,

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: I’d have you buy and sell so, so give alms,

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: Pray so; and, for the ord’ring your affairs,

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: To sing them too. When you do dance, I wish you

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: A wave o’ th’ sea, that you might ever do

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: Nothing but that, move still, still so,

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: And own no other function. Each your doing,

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: So singular in each particular,

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: Crowns what you are doing in the present deeds,

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: That all your acts are queens.

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: O Doricles,

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: Your praises are too large. But that your youth,

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: And the true blood which peeps fairly through ’t,

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: Do plainly give you out an unstained shepherd,

lines.text: With wisdom I might fear, my Doricles,

lines.text: I think you have

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL

lines.text: This is the prettiest low-born lass that ever

lines.text: Ran on the green-sward. Nothing she does or seems

lines.text: But smacks of something greater than herself,

lines.speaker: POLIXENES

lines.text: He tells her something

lines.text: That makes her blood look out. Good sooth, she is

lines.text: Now, in good time!

lines.speaker: CLOWN

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: Upon the water as he’ll stand and read,

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD

lines.text: I think there is not half a kiss to choose

lines.text: Who loves another best.

lines.text: O master, if you did but hear the pedlar at the door, you would never

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: dance again after a tabor and pipe; no, the bagpipe could not move you.

lines.text: He could never come better: he shall come in. I love a ballad but even

lines.text: too well, if it be doleful matter merrily set down, or a very pleasant

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: thing indeed and sung lamentably.

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: He hath songs for man or woman of all sizes. No milliner can so fit his

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: customers with gloves. He has the prettiest love-songs for maids, so

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: without bawdry, which is strange; with such delicate burdens of dildos

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: and fadings, “jump her and thump her”; and where some stretch-mouthed

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: rascal would, as it were, mean mischief and break a foul gap into the

lines.text: matter, he makes the maid to answer “Whoop, do me no harm, good man”;

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: puts him off, slights him, with “Whoop, do me no harm, good man.”

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: This is a brave fellow.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Believe me, thou talkest of an admirable conceited fellow. Has he any

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: unbraided wares?

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: He hath ribbons of all the colours i’ th’ rainbow; points, more than

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: all the lawyers in Bohemia can learnedly handle, though they come to

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: him by th’ gross; inkles, caddisses, cambrics, lawns; why he sings ’em

lines.text: over as they were gods or goddesses; you would think a smock were a

lines.text: she-angel, he so chants to the sleeve-hand and the work about the

lines.text: square on ’t.

lines.speaker: CLOWN

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: _Lawn as white as driven snow,

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: Cypress black as e’er was crow,

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: Gloves as sweet as damask roses,

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: Masks for faces and for noses,

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: Bugle-bracelet, necklace amber,

lines.text: Perfume for a lady’s chamber,

lines.text: Golden quoifs and stomachers

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: For my lads to give their dears,

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: Pins and poking-sticks of steel,

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: What maids lack from head to heel.

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: Come buy of me, come; come buy, come buy;

lines.text: If I were not in love with Mopsa, thou shouldst take no money of me;

lines.text: will shame you to give him again.

lines.text: Is there no manners left among maids? Will they wear their plackets

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: where they should bear their faces? Is there not milking-time, when you

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: are going to bed, or kiln-hole, to whistle of these secrets, but you

lines.text: must be tittle-tattling before all our guests? ’Tis well they are

lines.text: I have done. Come, you promised me a tawdry lace and a pair of sweet

lines.text: Have I not told thee how I was cozened by the way and lost all my

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: money?

lines.text: And indeed, sir, there are cozeners abroad; therefore it behoves men to

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: be wary.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Fear not thou, man. Thou shalt lose nothing here.

lines.text: I hope so, sir; for I have about me many parcels of charge.

lines.text: What hast here? Ballads?

lines.text: Pray now, buy some. I love a ballad in print alife, for then we are

lines.text: sure they are true.

lines.text: heads and toads carbonadoed.

lines.text: Is it true, think you?

lines.text: Come on, lay it by; and let’s first see more ballads. We’ll buy the

lines.text: other things anon.

lines.text: Here’s another ballad, of a fish that appeared upon the coast on

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: and sung this ballad against the hard hearts of maids. It was thought

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: she was a woman, and was turned into a cold fish for she would not

lines.text: exchange flesh with one that loved her. The ballad is very pitiful, and

lines.text: Is it true too, think you?

lines.text: Five justices’ hands at it, and witnesses more than my pack will hold.

lines.text: This is a merry ballad; but a very pretty one.

lines.text: Let’s have some merry ones.

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: request, I can tell you.

lines.text: We can both sing it: if thou’lt bear a part, thou shalt hear; ’tis in

lines.text: three parts.

lines.text: We had the tune on ’t a month ago.

lines.text: I can bear my part; you must know ’tis my occupation: have at it with

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: you.

lines.text: _Get you hence, for I must go

lines.text: Where it fits not you to know._

lines.speaker: MOPSA
lines.text: _O, whither?_

lines.text: _Neither._

lines.text: _Neither._

lines.text: The scene you play were mine. For instance, sir,

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: That you may know you shall not want,—one word.
[_They talk aside._]
Enter Autolycus.

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: Ha, ha! what a fool Honesty is! and Trust, his sworn brother, a very

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: simple gentleman! I have sold all my trumpery. Not a counterfeit stone,

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: not a ribbon, glass, pomander, brooch, table-book, ballad, knife, tape,

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: glove, shoe-tie, bracelet, horn-ring, to keep my pack from fasting.

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: They throng who should buy first, as if my trinkets had been hallowed

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: and brought a benediction to the buyer: by which means I saw whose

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: purse was best in picture; and what I saw, to my good use I remembered.

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: My clown (who wants but something to be a reasonable man) grew so in

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: love with the wenches’ song that he would not stir his pettitoes till

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: he had both tune and words; which so drew the rest of the herd to me

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: that all their other senses stuck in ears: you might have pinched a

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: placket, it was senseless; ’twas nothing to geld a codpiece of a purse;

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: I would have filed keys off that hung in chains: no hearing, no

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: feeling, but my sir’s song, and admiring the nothing of it. So that in

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: this time of lethargy I picked and cut most of their festival purses;

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: and had not the old man come in with a whoobub against his daughter and

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: the king’s son, and scared my choughs from the chaff, I had not left a

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: purse alive in the whole army.

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: Camillo, Florizel and Perdita come forward.

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: Nay, but my letters, by this means being there

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: So soon as you arrive, shall clear that doubt.

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: And those that you’ll procure from king Leontes?

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: Shall satisfy your father.

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: Happy be you!

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: All that you speak shows fair.
[_Seeing Autolycus._]

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: Who have we here?

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: We’ll make an instrument of this; omit

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: Nothing may give us aid.
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: If they have overheard me now,—why, hanging.

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: How now, good fellow! why shakest thou so? Fear not, man; here’s no

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: harm intended to thee.

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: I am a poor fellow, sir.

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: Why, be so still; here’s nobody will steal that from thee: yet, for the

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: outside of thy poverty we must make an exchange; therefore discase thee

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: instantly,—thou must think there’s a necessity in’t—and change garments

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: with this gentleman: though the pennyworth on his side be the worst,

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: yet hold thee, there’s some boot.
[_Giving money._]

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: I am a poor fellow, sir: [_Aside._] I know ye well enough.

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: Nay, prithee dispatch: the gentleman is half flayed already.

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: Are you in earnest, sir? [_Aside._] I smell the trick on’t.

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: Dispatch, I prithee.

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: Indeed, I have had earnest; but I cannot with conscience take it.

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: Unbuckle, unbuckle.
[_Florizel and Autolycus exchange garments._]

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: Fortunate mistress,—let my prophecy

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: Come home to you!—you must retire yourself

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: Into some covert. Take your sweetheart’s hat

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: And pluck it o’er your brows, muffle your face,

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: Dismantle you; and, as you can, disliken

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: The truth of your own seeming; that you may

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: (For I do fear eyes over) to shipboard

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: Get undescried.

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: I see the play so lies

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: That I must bear a part.

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: No remedy.

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: Have you done there?

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: Should I now meet my father,

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: He would not call me son.

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: Nay, you shall have no hat.
[_Giving it to Perdita._]

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: Come, lady, come. Farewell, my friend.

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: Adieu, sir.

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: O Perdita, what have we twain forgot?

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: Pray you a word.
[_They converse apart._]
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: What I do next, shall be to tell the king

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: Of this escape, and whither they are bound;

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: Wherein my hope is I shall so prevail

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: To force him after: in whose company

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: I shall re-view Sicilia; for whose sight

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: I have a woman’s longing.

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: Fortune speed us!

lines.speaker: FLORIZEL
lines.text: Thus we set on, Camillo, to the sea-side.

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: The swifter speed the better.
[_Exeunt Florizel, Perdita and Camillo._]

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: I understand the business, I hear it. To have an open ear, a quick eye,

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: and a nimble hand, is necessary for a cut-purse; a good nose is

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: requisite also, to smell out work for the other senses. I see this is

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: the time that the unjust man doth thrive. What an exchange had this

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: been without boot! What a boot is here with this exchange! Sure the

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: gods do this year connive at us, and we may do anything extempore. The

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: prince himself is about a piece of iniquity, stealing away from his

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: father with his clog at his heels: if I thought it were a piece of

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: honesty to acquaint the king withal, I would not do’t: I hold it the

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: more knavery to conceal it; and therein am I constant to my profession.
Enter Clown and Shepherd.

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: Aside, aside; here is more matter for a hot brain: every lane’s end,

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: every shop, church, session, hanging, yields a careful man work.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: See, see; what a man you are now! There is no other way but to tell the

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: king she’s a changeling, and none of your flesh and blood.

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: Nay, but hear me.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Nay, but hear me.

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: Go to, then.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: She being none of your flesh and blood, your flesh and blood has not

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: offended the king; and so your flesh and blood is not to be punished by

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: him. Show those things you found about her, those secret things, all

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: but what she has with her: this being done, let the law go whistle, I

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: warrant you.

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: I will tell the king all, every word, yea, and his son’s pranks too;

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: who, I may say, is no honest man neither to his father nor to me, to go

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: about to make me the king’s brother-in-law.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Indeed, brother-in-law was the farthest off you could have been to him,

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: and then your blood had been the dearer by I know how much an ounce.
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: Very wisely, puppies!

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: Well, let us to the king: there is that in this fardel will make him

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: scratch his beard.
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: I know not what impediment this complaint may be to the

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: flight of my master.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Pray heartily he be at’ palace.
[_Aside._]

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: Though I am not naturally honest, I am so sometimes by

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: chance. Let me pocket up my pedlar’s excrement. [_Takes off his false

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: beard._] How now, rustics! whither are you bound?

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: To the palace, an it like your worship.

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: Your affairs there, what, with whom, the condition of that fardel, the

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: place of your dwelling, your names, your ages, of what having,

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: breeding, and anything that is fitting to be known? discover!

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: We are but plain fellows, sir.

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: A lie; you are rough and hairy. Let me have no lying. It becomes none

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: but tradesmen, and they often give us soldiers the lie; but we pay them

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: for it with stamped coin, not stabbing steel; therefore they do not

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: give us the lie.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Your worship had like to have given us one, if you had not taken

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: yourself with the manner.

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: Are you a courtier, an ’t like you, sir?

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: Whether it like me or no, I am a courtier. Seest thou not the air of

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: the court in these enfoldings? hath not my gait in it the measure of

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: the court? receives not thy nose court-odour from me? reflect I not on

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: thy baseness court-contempt? Think’st thou, for that I insinuate, or

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: toaze from thee thy business, I am therefore no courtier? I am courtier

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: _cap-a-pe_, and one that will either push on or pluck back thy business

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: there. Whereupon I command thee to open thy affair.

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: My business, sir, is to the king.

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: What advocate hast thou to him?

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: I know not, an ’t like you.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Advocate’s the court-word for a pheasant. Say you have none.

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: None, sir; I have no pheasant, cock nor hen.

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: How bless’d are we that are not simple men!

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: Yet nature might have made me as these are,

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: Therefore I will not disdain.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: This cannot be but a great courtier.

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: His garments are rich, but he wears them not handsomely.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: He seems to be the more noble in being fantastical: a great man, I’ll

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: warrant; I know by the picking on’s teeth.

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: The fardel there? What’s i’ th’ fardel? Wherefore that box?

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: Sir, there lies such secrets in this fardel and box which none must

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: know but the king; and which he shall know within this hour, if I may

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: come to th’ speech of him.

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: Age, thou hast lost thy labour.

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: Why, sir?

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: The king is not at the palace; he is gone aboard a new ship to purge

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: melancholy and air himself: for, if thou beest capable of things

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: serious, thou must know the king is full of grief.

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: So ’tis said, sir; about his son, that should have married a shepherd’s

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: daughter.

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: If that shepherd be not in hand-fast, let him fly. The curses he shall

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: have, the tortures he shall feel, will break the back of man, the heart

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: of monster.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Think you so, sir?

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: Not he alone shall suffer what wit can make heavy and vengeance bitter;

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: but those that are germane to him, though removed fifty times, shall

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: all come under the hangman: which, though it be great pity, yet it is

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: necessary. An old sheep-whistling rogue, a ram-tender, to offer to have

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: his daughter come into grace! Some say he shall be stoned; but that

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: death is too soft for him, say I. Draw our throne into a sheepcote! All

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: deaths are too few, the sharpest too easy.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Has the old man e’er a son, sir, do you hear, an ’t like you, sir?

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: He has a son, who shall be flayed alive; then ’nointed over with honey,

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: set on the head of a wasp’s nest; then stand till he be three quarters

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: and a dram dead; then recovered again with aqua-vitæ or some other hot

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: infusion; then, raw as he is, and in the hottest day prognostication

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: proclaims, shall he be set against a brick wall, the sun looking with a

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: southward eye upon him, where he is to behold him with flies blown to

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: death. But what talk we of these traitorly rascals, whose miseries are

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: to be smiled at, their offences being so capital? Tell me (for you seem

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: to be honest plain men) what you have to the king. Being something

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: gently considered, I’ll bring you where he is aboard, tender your

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: persons to his presence, whisper him in your behalfs; and if it be in

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: man besides the king to effect your suits, here is man shall do it.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: He seems to be of great authority: close with him, give him gold; and

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: though authority be a stubborn bear, yet he is oft led by the nose with

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: gold: show the inside of your purse to the outside of his hand, and no

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: more ado. Remember: “ston’d” and “flayed alive”.

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: An ’t please you, sir, to undertake the business for us, here is that

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: gold I have. I’ll make it as much more, and leave this young man in

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: pawn till I bring it you.

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: After I have done what I promised?

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: Ay, sir.

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: Well, give me the moiety. Are you a party in this business?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: In some sort, sir: but though my case be a pitiful one, I hope I shall

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: not be flayed out of it.

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: O, that’s the case of the shepherd’s son. Hang him, he’ll be made an

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: example.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Comfort, good comfort! We must to the king and show our strange sights.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: He must know ’tis none of your daughter nor my sister; we are gone

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: else. Sir, I will give you as much as this old man does when the

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: business is performed, and remain, as he says, your pawn till it be

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: brought you.

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: I will trust you. Walk before toward the sea-side; go on the

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: right-hand. I will but look upon the hedge, and follow you.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: We are blessed in this man, as I may say, even blessed.

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: Let’s before, as he bids us. He was provided to do us good.
[_Exeunt Shepherd and Clown._]

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: If I had a mind to be honest, I see Fortune would not suffer me: she

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: drops booties in my mouth. I am courted now with a double occasion:

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: gold, and a means to do the prince my master good; which who knows how

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: that may turn back to my advancement? I will bring these two moles,

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: these blind ones, aboard him. If he think it fit to shore them again

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: and that the complaint they have to the king concerns him nothing, let

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: him call me rogue for being so far officious; for I am proof against

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: that title and what shame else belongs to ’t. To him will I present

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: them. There may be matter in it.
[_Exit._]

scenes.setting: Sicilia. A Room in the palace of Leontes.

lines.text: Enter Leontes, Cleomenes, Dion, Paulina and others.

CLEOMENES Sir, you have done enough, and have perform’d A saint-like sorrow: no fault could you make Which you have not redeem’d; indeed, paid down More penitence than done trespass: at the last, Do as the heavens have done, forget your evil; With them, forgive yourself.

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: Whilst I remember

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: Her and her virtues, I cannot forget

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: My blemishes in them; and so still think of

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: The wrong I did myself: which was so much

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: That heirless it hath made my kingdom, and

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: Destroy’d the sweet’st companion that e’er man

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: Bred his hopes out of.

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: True, too true, my lord.

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: If, one by one, you wedded all the world,

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Or from the all that are took something good,

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: To make a perfect woman, she you kill’d

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Would be unparallel’d.

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: I think so. Kill’d!

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: She I kill’d! I did so: but thou strik’st me

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: Sorely, to say I did: it is as bitter

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: Upon thy tongue as in my thought. Now, good now,

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: Say so but seldom.

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: CLEOMENES

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: Not at all, good lady.

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: You might have spoken a thousand things that would

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: Have done the time more benefit and grac’d

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: Your kindness better.

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: You are one of those

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Would have him wed again.

lines.speaker: DION
lines.text: If you would not so,

lines.speaker: DION
lines.text: You pity not the state, nor the remembrance

lines.speaker: DION
lines.text: Of his most sovereign name; consider little

lines.speaker: DION
lines.text: What dangers, by his highness’ fail of issue,

lines.speaker: DION
lines.text: May drop upon his kingdom, and devour

lines.speaker: DION
lines.text: Incertain lookers-on. What were more holy

lines.speaker: DION
lines.text: Than to rejoice the former queen is well?

lines.speaker: DION
lines.text: What holier than, for royalty’s repair,

lines.speaker: DION
lines.text: For present comfort, and for future good,

lines.speaker: DION
lines.text: To bless the bed of majesty again

lines.speaker: DION
lines.text: With a sweet fellow to ’t?

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: There is none worthy,

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Respecting her that’s gone. Besides, the gods

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Will have fulfill’d their secret purposes;

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: For has not the divine Apollo said,

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Is ’t not the tenor of his oracle,

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: That king Leontes shall not have an heir

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Till his lost child be found? Which that it shall,

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Is all as monstrous to our human reason

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: As my Antigonus to break his grave

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: And come again to me; who, on my life,

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Did perish with the infant. ’Tis your counsel

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: My lord should to the heavens be contrary,

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Oppose against their wills. [_To Leontes._] Care not for issue;

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: The crown will find an heir. Great Alexander

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Left his to th’ worthiest; so his successor

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Was like to be the best.

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: Good Paulina,

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: Who hast the memory of Hermione,

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: I know, in honour, O that ever I

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: Had squar’d me to thy counsel! Then, even now,

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: I might have look’d upon my queen’s full eyes,

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: Have taken treasure from her lips,—

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: And left them

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: More rich for what they yielded.

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: Thou speak’st truth.

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: No more such wives; therefore, no wife: one worse,

lines.speaker: LEONTES

lines.speaker: SECOND GENTLEMAN
lines.text: visited that removed house. Shall we thither, and with our company

lines.speaker: SECOND GENTLEMAN
lines.text: piece the rejoicing?

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: Who would be thence that has the benefit of access? Every wink of an

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: eye some new grace will be born. Our absence makes us unthrifty to our

lines.speaker: FIRST GENTLEMAN
lines.text: knowledge. Let’s along.
[_Exeunt Gentlemen._]

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: Now, had I not the dash of my former life in me, would preferment drop

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: on my head. I brought the old man and his son aboard the prince; told

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: him I heard them talk of a fardel and I know not what. But he at that

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: time over-fond of the shepherd’s daughter (so he then took her to be),

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: who began to be much sea-sick, and himself little better, extremity of

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: weather continuing, this mystery remained undiscover’d. But ’tis all

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: one to me; for had I been the finder-out of this secret, it would not

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: have relish’d among my other discredits.
Enter Shepherd and Clown.

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: Here come those I have done good to against my will, and already

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: appearing in the blossoms of their fortune.

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: Come, boy; I am past more children, but thy sons and daughters will be

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: all gentlemen born.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: You are well met, sir. You denied to fight with me this other day,

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: because I was no gentleman born. See you these clothes? Say you see

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: them not and think me still no gentleman born: you were best say these

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: robes are not gentlemen born. Give me the lie, do; and try whether I am

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: not now a gentleman born.

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: I know you are now, sir, a gentleman born.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Ay, and have been so any time these four hours.

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: And so have I, boy!

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: So you have: but I was a gentleman born before my father; for the

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: king’s son took me by the hand and called me brother; and then the two

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: kings called my father brother; and then the prince, my brother, and

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: the princess, my sister, called my father father; and so we wept; and

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: there was the first gentleman-like tears that ever we shed.

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: We may live, son, to shed many more.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Ay; or else ’twere hard luck, being in so preposterous estate as we

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: are.

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: I humbly beseech you, sir, to pardon me all the faults I have committed

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: to your worship, and to give me your good report to the prince my

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: master.

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: Prithee, son, do; for we must be gentle, now we are gentlemen.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Thou wilt amend thy life?

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: Ay, an it like your good worship.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Give me thy hand: I will swear to the prince thou art as honest a true

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: fellow as any is in Bohemia.

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: You may say it, but not swear it.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Not swear it, now I am a gentleman? Let boors and franklins say it,

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: I’ll swear it.

lines.speaker: SHEPHERD
lines.text: How if it be false, son?

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: If it be ne’er so false, a true gentleman may swear it in the behalf of

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: his friend. And I’ll swear to the prince thou art a tall fellow of thy

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: hands and that thou wilt not be drunk; but I know thou art no tall

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: fellow of thy hands and that thou wilt be drunk: but I’ll swear it; and

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: I would thou wouldst be a tall fellow of thy hands.

lines.speaker: AUTOLYCUS
lines.text: I will prove so, sir, to my power.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Ay, by any means, prove a tall fellow: if I do not wonder how thou

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: dar’st venture to be drunk, not being a tall fellow, trust me not.

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: Hark! the kings and the princes, our kindred, are going to see the

lines.speaker: CLOWN
lines.text: queen’s picture. Come, follow us: we’ll be thy good masters.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: The same. A Room in Paulina’s house.

lines.text: That I have had of thee!

lines.text: What, sovereign sir,

lines.text: I did not well, I meant well. All my services

lines.text: You have paid home: but that you have vouchsaf’d,

lines.text: With your crown’d brother and these your contracted

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Heirs of your kingdoms, my poor house to visit,

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: It is a surplus of your grace which never

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: My life may last to answer.

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: O Paulina,

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: We honour you with trouble. But we came

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: To see the statue of our queen: your gallery

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: Have we pass’d through, not without much content

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: In many singularities; but we saw not

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: That which my daughter came to look upon,

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: The statue of her mother.

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: As she liv’d peerless,

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: So her dead likeness, I do well believe,

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Excels whatever yet you look’d upon

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Or hand of man hath done; therefore I keep it

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Lonely, apart. But here it is: prepare

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: To see the life as lively mock’d as ever

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Still sleep mock’d death. Behold, and say ’tis well.

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Paulina undraws a curtain, and discovers Hermione standing as a

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: statue.

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: I like your silence, it the more shows off

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Your wonder: but yet speak. First you, my liege.

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Comes it not something near?

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: Her natural posture!

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: Chide me, dear stone, that I may say indeed

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: Thou art Hermione; or rather, thou art she

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: In thy not chiding; for she was as tender

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: As infancy and grace. But yet, Paulina,

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: Hermione was not so much wrinkled, nothing

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: So aged as this seems.

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: O, not by much!

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: So much the more our carver’s excellence,

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Which lets go by some sixteen years and makes her

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: As she liv’d now.

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: As now she might have done,

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: So much to my good comfort as it is

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: Now piercing to my soul. O, thus she stood,

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: Even with such life of majesty, warm life,

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: As now it coldly stands, when first I woo’d her!

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: I am asham’d: does not the stone rebuke me

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: For being more stone than it? O royal piece,

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: There’s magic in thy majesty, which has

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: My evils conjur’d to remembrance and

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: From thy admiring daughter took the spirits,

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: Standing like stone with thee.

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: And give me leave,

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: And do not say ’tis superstition, that

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: I kneel, and then implore her blessing. Lady,

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: Dear queen, that ended when I but began,

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: Give me that hand of yours to kiss.

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: O, patience!

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: The statue is but newly fix’d, the colour’s

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Not dry.

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: My lord, your sorrow was too sore laid on,

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: Which sixteen winters cannot blow away,

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: So many summers dry. Scarce any joy

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: Did ever so long live; no sorrow

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: But kill’d itself much sooner.

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: Dear my brother,

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: Let him that was the cause of this have power

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: To take off so much grief from you as he

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: Will piece up in himself.

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Indeed, my lord,

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: If I had thought the sight of my poor image

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Would thus have wrought you—for the stone is mine—

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: I’d not have show’d it.

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: Do not draw the curtain.

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: No longer shall you gaze on’t, lest your fancy

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: May think anon it moves.

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: Let be, let be.

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: Would I were dead, but that methinks already—

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: What was he that did make it? See, my lord,

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: Would you not deem it breath’d? And that those veins

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: Did verily bear blood?

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: Masterly done:

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: The very life seems warm upon her lip.

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: The fixture of her eye has motion in ’t,

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: As we are mock’d with art.

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: I’ll draw the curtain:

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: My lord’s almost so far transported that

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: He’ll think anon it lives.

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: O sweet Paulina,

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: Make me to think so twenty years together!

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: No settled senses of the world can match

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: The pleasure of that madness. Let ’t alone.

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: I am sorry, sir, I have thus far stirr’d you: but

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: I could afflict you further.

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: Do, Paulina;

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: For this affliction has a taste as sweet

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: As any cordial comfort. Still methinks

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: There is an air comes from her. What fine chisel

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: Could ever yet cut breath? Let no man mock me,

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: For I will kiss her!

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Good my lord, forbear:

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: The ruddiness upon her lip is wet;

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: You’ll mar it if you kiss it, stain your own

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: With oily painting. Shall I draw the curtain?

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: No, not these twenty years.

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: So long could I

lines.speaker: PERDITA
lines.text: Stand by, a looker on.

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Either forbear,

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Quit presently the chapel, or resolve you

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: For more amazement. If you can behold it,

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: I’ll make the statue move indeed, descend,

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: And take you by the hand. But then you’ll think

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: (Which I protest against) I am assisted

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: By wicked powers.

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: What you can make her do

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: I am content to look on: what to speak,

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: I am content to hear; for ’tis as easy

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: To make her speak as move.

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: It is requir’d

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: You do awake your faith. Then all stand still;

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Or those that think it is unlawful business

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: I am about, let them depart.

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: Proceed:

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: No foot shall stir.

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Music, awake her: strike!
[_Music._]

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: ’Tis time; descend; be stone no more; approach;

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Strike all that look upon with marvel. Come;

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: I’ll fill your grave up: stir; nay, come away.

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Bequeath to death your numbness, for from him

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Dear life redeems you. You perceive she stirs.

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Hermione comes down from the pedestal.

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Start not; her actions shall be holy as

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: You hear my spell is lawful. Do not shun her

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Until you see her die again; for then

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: You kill her double. Nay, present your hand:

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: When she was young you woo’d her; now in age

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Is she become the suitor?
[_Embracing her._]

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: O, she’s warm!

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: If this be magic, let it be an art

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: Lawful as eating.

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: She embraces him.

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: She hangs about his neck.

lines.speaker: CAMILLO
lines.text: If she pertain to life, let her speak too.

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: Ay, and make it manifest where she has liv’d,

lines.speaker: POLIXENES
lines.text: Or how stol’n from the dead.

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: That she is living,

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Were it but told you, should be hooted at

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Like an old tale; but it appears she lives,

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Though yet she speak not. Mark a little while.

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Please you to interpose, fair madam. Kneel

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: And pray your mother’s blessing. Turn, good lady,

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Our Perdita is found.
[_Presenting Perdita who kneels to Hermione._]

lines.speaker: HERMIONE
lines.text: You gods, look down,

lines.speaker: HERMIONE
lines.text: And from your sacred vials pour your graces

lines.speaker: HERMIONE
lines.text: Upon my daughter’s head! Tell me, mine own,

lines.speaker: HERMIONE
lines.text: Where hast thou been preserv’d? where liv’d? how found

lines.speaker: HERMIONE
lines.text: Thy father’s court? for thou shalt hear that I,

lines.text: Knowing by Paulina that the oracle

lines.speaker: HERMIONE
lines.text: Gave hope thou wast in being, have preserv’d

lines.speaker: HERMIONE
lines.text: Myself to see the issue.

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: There’s time enough for that;

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Lest they desire upon this push to trouble

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Your joys with like relation. Go together,

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: You precious winners all; your exultation

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Partake to everyone. I, an old turtle,

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Will wing me to some wither’d bough, and there

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: My mate, that’s never to be found again,

lines.speaker: PAULINA
lines.text: Lament till I am lost.

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: O peace, Paulina!

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: Thou shouldst a husband take by my consent,

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: As I by thine a wife: this is a match,

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: And made between ’s by vows. Thou hast found mine;

lines.speaker: LEONTES
lines.text: But how, is to be question’d; for I saw her,

lines.speaker: LEONTES

lines.text: And take her by the hand, whose worth and honesty

lines.speaker: LEONTES
